newsitem.title: THAILAND: NAP's Chavalit says discussing new Thai government.
newsitem.headline: NAP's Chavalit says discussing new Thai government.

text.p: The leader of Thailand's New Aspiration Party (NAP), which narrowly won the country's general election, said on Monday a new coalition government would be formed within the next few days.
Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, NAP leader and the man likely to be next prime minister, said talks were taking place to decide the formation of the new government following Sunday's election.
"Probably not long. It will be completed within the next few days," he told a local radio station when asked when the new government would be set up.
Chavalit, whose NAP won 125 seats against 123 for the rival Democrat Party, appeared with leaders of four other political parties late on Sunday in a show of unity and said they could work together.

The four parties were the Chart Thai party of departing prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa which won 39 seats, the Prachakorn Thai with 18 seats, Social Action Party with 20 and the Muanchon Party with two seats.
The NAP and the four other parties would have a majority of 204 seats in parliament and be able to form a government, analysts said.
Chavalit stressed it was important that his cabinet be acceptable to the public.

"The five parties simply got together to have a chat. However, we cannot leave the people uncertain and aimless. We also listened to public opinions while checking the election results. It is normal for us to meet for discussions or cooperation," he said.
News of the NAP's victory and a potential alliance with the four parties who were partners in the troubled departing Banharn administration caused the Thai stock market to plummet on Monday morning.
Thai stocks fell by more than six percent in early trade. The index was down 5.85 percent or off 58.54 points at 942.19 at 0410 GMT.
Brokers said investors sold stocks because they viewed the impending coalition to be tainted with the negative image attached to the Banharn administration.
